22297-the-coast-of-bohemia.creator: W. D. Howells
22297-the-coast-of-bohemia.description: A book by W. D. Howells. hought, 'What a good thing it would be to have a nice village girl, with a real but limited gift, go from here to study art in New York! And married!' Cornelia and her mother at once stepped out of the inchoate; Ludlow advanced from another quarter of Chaos, and I began really to be.

arxiv-1510-08475.title: Saturation and geometrical scaling – from small x x deep inelastic ep scattering to high energy proton-proton and heavy ion collisions Presented at the XXIII International Workshop on Deep Inelastic Scattering and Related Subjects April 27 - May 1, 2015, Southern Methodist University, Dallas, Texas
arxiv-1510-08475.creator: Michal Praszalowicz
arxiv-1510-08475.description: Abstract Gluon distributions of colliding hadrons saturate as a result of the non-linear evolution equations of QCD. As a consequence there exists the so called saturation momentum, which is related to the gluon density per unit rapidity per transverse area. When saturation momentum is the only scale for physical processes, different observables exhibit geometrical scaling (GS).

arxiv-2103-03408.title: The curvature-induced gauge potential and the geometric momentum for a particle on a hypersphere
arxiv-2103-03408.creator: Z. Li, L. Q. Lai, Y. Zhong, Q. H. Liu
arxiv-2103-03408.description: Abstract A particle that is constrained to freely move on a hyperspherical surface in an N ( ≥ 2 ) N\left(\geq 2\right) dimensional flat space experiences a curvature-induced gauge potential, whose form was given long ago (J. Math. Phys. 34 (1993)2827).

arxiv-2107-11490.title: Local Group timing argument and virial theorem mass estimators from cosmological simulations 2021 Local Group timing argument and virial theorem mass estimators from cosmological simulations – References
arxiv-2107-11490.creator: Odelia V. Hartl, Louis E. Strigari
arxiv-2107-11490.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Odelia V. Hartl, Louis E. Strigari. We identify Local Group (LG) analogs in the IllustrisTNG cosmological simulation, and use these to study two mass estimators for the LG: one based on the timing argument (TA) and one based on the virial theorem (VT).

arxiv-2108-07546.title: Modified gravity models for inflation: In conformity with observations
arxiv-2108-07546.description: Abstract We consider a modified gravity framework for inflation by adding to the Einstein-Hilbert action a direct f ⁡ ( ϕ ) ​ T f(\phi)T term, where ϕ \phi is identified as the inflaton and T T is the trace of the energy-momentum tensor. The framework goes to Einstein gravity naturally when the inflaton decays out.

arxiv-2112-00928.title: Curvature dependences of wave propagation in reaction–diffusion models
arxiv-2112-00928.creator: Pascal R Buenzli a , {a,}, Matthew J Simpson a {a}
arxiv-2112-00928.description: Abstract Reaction–diffusion waves in multiple spatial dimensions advance at a rate that strongly depends on the curvature of the wave fronts. These waves have important applications in many physical, ecological, and biological systems. In this work, we analyse curvature dependences of travelling fronts in a single reaction–diffusion equation with general reaction term.

arxiv-2112-02412.title: Making Access Control Easy in IoT
arxiv-2112-02412.creator: Vafa Andalibi, Jayati Dev, DongInn Kim, Eliot Lear, L. Jean Camp
arxiv-2112-02412.description: Abstract Secure installation of Internet of Things (IoT) devices requires configuring access control correctly for each device. In order to enable correct configuration the Manufacturer Usage Description (MUD) has been developed by Internet Engineering Task Force (IETF) to automate the protection of IoT devices by micro-segmentation using dynamic access control lists.

arxiv-2209-08840.title: Number of paths in a graph
arxiv-2209-08840.creator: Ivan Jokić, Piet Van Mieghem
arxiv-2209-08840.description: Abstract The k k -th power of the adjacency matrix of a simple undirected graph represents the number of walks with length k k between pairs of nodes. As a walk where no node repeats, a path is a walk where each node is only visited once. The set of paths constitutes a relatively small subset of all possible walks.

arxiv-2210-00024.title: New tools for dissecting the general 2HDM
arxiv-2210-00024.creator: Henning Bahl, Marcela Carena, Nina M. Coyle, Aurora Ireland, Carlos E.M. Wagner
arxiv-2210-00024.description: Abstract Two Higgs doublet models (2HDM) provide the low energy effective theory (EFT) description in many well motivated extensions of the Standard Model. It is therefore relevant to study their properties, as well as the theoretical constraints on these models.

arxiv-2301-09367.title: Sequencings in Semidirect Products via the Polynomial Method
arxiv-2301-09367.creator: S. Costa, S. Della Fiore, M. A. Ollis

arxiv-2403-02723.title: Minimum Topology Attacks for Graph Neural Networks
arxiv-2403-02723.creator: Mengmei Zhang, Xiao Wang, Chuan Shi, Lingjuan Lyu, Tianchi Yang, Junping Du
arxiv-2403-02723.description: Abstract . With the great popularity of Graph Neural Networks (GNNs), their robustness to adversarial topology attacks has received significant attention. Although many attack methods have been proposed, they mainly focus on fixed-budget attacks, aiming at finding the most adversarial perturbations within a fixed budget for target node.

Replacement of infarcted heart tissue with regenerating myocardium from endogenous progenitor pools or exogenously introduced stem cells remains a therapeutic ideal. Th

pmc-10533590.title: Association of pre-diagnostic physical exercise and peri-diagnostic body composition with mortality in non-metastatic colorectal cancer
pmc-10533590.creator: David Renman, Bethany van Guelpen, Fredrick Anderson, Jan Axelsson, Katrine Riklund, Karin Strigård, Richard Palmqvist, Ulf Gunnarsson, Björn Gylling
pmc-10533590.description: PurposeSarcopenia and myosteatosis, quantified via computed tomography (CT), are associated with poor colorectal cancer outcomes. These body composition estimates can be influenced by physical exercise. We explored the correlation between pre-diagnostic physical exercise, body composition close to diagnosis, and the combined prognosis impact of these factors.

pmc-10693117.title: A rapid and stable spontaneous reprogramming system of Spermatogonial stem cells to Pluripotent State
pmc-10693117.creator: Rui Wei, Xiaoyu Zhang, Xiaoxiao Li, Jian Wen, Hongyang Liu, Jiqiang Fu, Li Li, Wenyi Zhang, Zhen Liu, Yang Yang, Kang Zou
pmc-10693117.description: BackgroundThe scarcity of pluripotent stem cells poses a major challenge to the clinical application, given ethical and biosafety considerations. While germline stem cells commit to gamete differentiation throughout life, studies demonstrated the spontaneous acquisition of pluripotency by spermatogonial stem cells (SSCs) from neonatal testes at a low frequency (1 in 1.5 × 107).

pmc-11355438.title: Demineralized Dentin Matrix Incorporated with rhBMP-2 Composite Graft for Treating Medication-Related Osteonecrosis of the Jaw
pmc-11355438.creator: Jeong-Kui Ku, Jin-Won Choi, Seung-Min Song, Pil-Young Yun, In-Woong Um, Dae Ho Leem
pmc-11355438.description: Medication-Related Osteonecrosis of the Jaw (MRONJ) is characterized by bone exposure in the oral and maxillofacial region for more than eight weeks in patients treated with anti-resorptive agents, immunosuppressants, or anti-angiogenic agents, without prior radiation therapy or metastatic disease to the jaws. Conservative treatments can control infection in mild cases, but surgical intervention is necessary for patients with severe symptoms.

pmc-11389592.title: Effort–reward imbalance and well-being among psychiatric nurses: the mediating role of burnout and decent work
pmc-11389592.creator: Xiaoyan Zhang, Liya Zhang, Bowen Xue, Yanping Li, Mengmeng Yan, Hong Luo, Xiaoyu Huang
pmc-11389592.description: BackgroundPsychiatric nurses face additional challenges due to negative perceptions, workplace violence, and a lack of respect, impacting their well-being and job satisfaction, which are crucial for improving psychiatric care and patient outcomes.ObjectivesThis study aims to examine the relationship between effort-reward imbalance, well-being, burnout, and decent work among psychiatric nurses.MethodsThis study used a cross-sectional design.

pmc-11487292.title: Atypical Imaging Findings in a Cortisol-producing Adrenal Adenoma Predominantly Composed of Lipid-poor Compact Cells
pmc-11487292.creator: Satoshi Kawata, Yoshinari Obata, Aya Akai-Samoto, Kosuke Mukai, Kazuyuki Miyashita, Iichiro Shimomura
pmc-11487292.description: Cortisol-producing adrenal adenomas consist of a mixture of lipid-rich clear and lipid-poor compact cells in varying proportions. Most adenomas are mainly composed of lipid-rich clear cells and typically exhibit low computed tomography (CT) attenuation values, high uptake on 131I-adosterol scintigraphy, and mild accumulation on 18F-fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography/CT.

pmc-11651626.title: Evolution of two metabolic genes involved in nucleotide and amino acid metabolism in Pseudomonas aeruginosa
pmc-11651626.creator: Yutong Wu, Yuqi Shi, Xiaohui Liang, Rajesh P. Shastry, Rajesh P. Shastry, Rajesh P. Shastry
pmc-11651626.description: Pseudomonas aeruginosa is an opportunistic human pathogen causing various severe infections. Understanding genetic mechanisms of its metabolic versatility aids in developing novel antibacterial drugs and therapeutic strategies to address multidrug-resistant P. aeruginosa infections. The metabolism of nucleotides and amino acids contributes to the cycle of two key biological macromolecules in the genetic central dogma.

pmc-11888730.title: Comparative Evaluation of Shear Bond Strength of Orthodontic Metal Bracket Bonded with the Conventional Adhesive System and Moisture Insensitive Primer System on a Tooth Surface Which has Undergone Bleaching with 35% Hydrogen Peroxide – An In Vitro Study
pmc-11888730.creator: Praveen Roy, KK Manjusha, A Nishad, Ashitha Aravindan, JK Krishnajith, KA Jameema
pmc-11888730.description: Background and Objectives:Today, orthodontic bracket bonding on the tooth surface is a vital phase in any orthodontic therapy as strong tooth-bracket bonding is essential for success and efficiency. Tooth whitening is popular due to tooth discolouration and patient need for esthetic changes.

pmc-12394944.title: Can super resolution via deep learning improve classification accuracy in dental radiography?
pmc-12394944.creator: Berrin Çelik, Mahsa Mikaeili, Mehmet Z Genç, Mahmut E Çelik
pmc-12394944.description: ObjectivesDeep learning-driven super resolution (SR) aims to enhance the quality and resolution of images, offering potential benefits in dental imaging. Although extensive research has focused on deep learning based dental classification tasks, the impact of applying SR techniques on classification remains underexplored.

pmc-12395932.title: Ultrasonographic and CBCT analysis of foreign bodies and dental materials
pmc-12395932.creator: Hasret Yuce, Gozde Acikgoz
pmc-12395932.description: BackgroundTo reveal the radiodensity and sonographic characteristics of various foreign bodies and dental materials to aid in the diagnosis of these materials.MethodsThe study included 41 objects consisting of various foreign bodies and dental materials. The objects were examined by embedding them in bovine gelatin, an in vitro environment and their radiodensity was evaluated using cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT).

pmc-12466719.title: Post-Traumatic Growth in University Students After Earthquakes: The Effect of Perceived Social Support and Psychological Resilience
pmc-12466719.creator: Ferhat Toper, Rauf Yanardağ, Mehmet Koca, Veysi Baydar, Caroline S Clauss-Ehlers
pmc-12466719.description: This quantitative study examined the relationships between perceived social support, psychological resilience, and posttraumatic growth (PTG) among university students affected by the 6 February 2023 earthquakes in Türkiye. Utilizing a correlational design, the study tested whether psychological resilience mediated the relationship between perceived social support and PTG.

pmc-12501849.title: Design, synthesis and evaluation of arylpurine-based sinefungin mimetics as zika virus methyltransferase inhibitors
pmc-12501849.creator: Natalia del Río, Iván Arribas-Álvarez, José-María Orduña, Priscila Sutto-Ortiz, Johan Neyts, Suzanne Kaptein, Etienne Decroly, Eva-María Priego, María-Jesús Pérez-Pérez
pmc-12501849.description: Arylpurine derivatives were designed and synthesized to mimic sinefungin by targeting the SAM/SAH binding site of zika virus (ZIKV) methyltransferase (MTase). These compounds incorporate adenine or 6-methyl-7-deazapurine bases, while the ribose of sinefungin has been replaced by an aniline, linked to its amino acid chain via a CO or a CH2 unit.

pmc-12593482.title: Arterial stiffness after 6 weeks postdelivery in women with a history of hypertensive disorders of pregnancy: a systematic review and meta-analysis
pmc-12593482.creator: Xolani B. Mbongozi, Stuart D. R. Galloway, Angus M. Hunter, Jean Paul M. Milambo, Charles B. Businge
pmc-12593482.description: IntroductionThe main objective of this systematic review was to determine if the arterial stiffness remains elevated after 6 weeks post-delivery in women with a history of hypertensive disorders of pregnancy (HDP).Methods and analysisA comprehensive systematic literature search was conducted across multiple electronic databases, including Medline, PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library, Google Scholar, Web of Science, and CINAHL.

pmc-13099899.title: Gamification in health education: a mini-review of engagement strategies for the smartphone generation
pmc-13099899.creator: John Matkovic
pmc-13099899.description: Smartphones and social media use among young adults is at an all-time high, and research has linked non-academic use to reduced long-term retention and exam performance. Students often perceive device use as a social device with little to no risk to their academic success, while social norms research documents frequent misperceptions of peer smartphone behaviors.

pmc-13263597.title: Total Sanghuangporus vaninii Extract Ameliorates Cisplatin-Induced Glioma Cell Death by Regulating Ferroptosis and Inflammation
pmc-13263597.creator: Yankai Xu, Jiesi Zhou, Xiaobin Zhou, Yong Li, Senyuan Yang, Zebin Xue
pmc-13263597.description: ObjectivesFerroptosis is a distinct form of programmed cell death characterized by iron (Fe)-dependent oxidative stress and the accumulation of intracellular reactive oxygen species. Cisplatin (CPT), a chemotherapeutic agent, can induce ferroptosis in glioma cells and act synergistically with erastin (EST). The total extract of the fungus Sanghuangporus vaninii (TSV) has anticancer and antioxidant activities.

pmc-13296575.title: Photosynthetic Behavior of Wheat in Reclaimed Fly Ash Amended Soil—Probed by MINI‐PAM (Photosynthetic Yield Analyzer)
pmc-13296575.creator: Chandralekha Piparia, Anjali Verma, Santosh Kumar Prajapati
pmc-13296575.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Fly ash (FA) management is a global environmental concern. Although FA has been widely studied as a soil amendment to improve crop growth and productivity, its utilization remains limited due to the presence of toxic heavy metals (HMs). Reclamation of FA using tolerant plant species is a sustainable strategy to mitigate adverse environmental effects and improve its suitability as a soil mulcher. However, studies evaluating the use of reclaimed fly ash (RFA) as a soil amendment remain limited.

pmc-13336721.title: Pharmacological Inhibition of FKBP51 Mitigates Early Life Adversity‐Induced Social Deficits in Male Mice
pmc-13336721.creator: Joeri Bordes, Xiuqi Ji, Serena Gasperoni, Choham Sudre‐Chinsky, Amirali Kalbasi, Daniela Harbich, Cornelia Flachskamm, Paula Fontanet, Sowmya Narayan, Manfred Uhr, Christian Namendorf, Camilla Bellone, Alon Chen, Felix Hausch, Juan Pablo Lopez, Mathias V Schmidt
pmc-13336721.description: Early life adversity (ELA) is a major risk factor for psychiatric disorders, but targeted preventative strategies are lacking due to poor mechanistic insight. The FKBP51 protein, a co‐chaperone of the glucocorticoid receptor, is a key mediator of stress vulnerability. We tested if pharmacological inhibition of FKBP51 with the selective inhibitor SAFit2 prevents the long‐term consequences of ELA.

pmc-13347817.title: Early blood pressure lowering and cerebral oedema in thrombolysis-treated stroke: secondary analysis of the ENCHANTED trial
pmc-13347817.creator: Feifeng Liu, Xinwen Ren, Chen Chen, Menglu Ouyang, Qiang Li, Xia Wang, Guobin Zhang, Luyun Zhang, Leibo Liu, Shoujiang You, Richard I Lindley, Thompson Robinson, Yi Sui, Gang Li, Craig Anderson, Lili Song, on behalf of the ENCHANTED Investigators
pmc-13347817.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Background and purposeControversy persists over the balance of benefits and harms of early intensive blood pressure (BP) lowering in thrombolysis-treated acute ischaemic stroke (AIS) patients. The BP-control arm of the Enhanced Control of Hypertension and Thrombolysis Stroke Study (ENCHANTED) (n=2196) showed that compared with guideline-recommended management (systolic BP (SBP)<180 mm Hg), intensive BP lowering did not improve functional outcome despite reducing intracranial haemorrhage.

pmc-13350347.title: Severe Toxicosis Secondary to Accidental Oclacitinib Ingestion in Three Cats
pmc-13350347.creator: Jessica Kielb Basile, Sara C. Lister
pmc-13350347.description: ObjectiveTo describe the clinical course, outcome, necropsy findings, possible mechanisms of toxicosis, and treatment implications for three cats with acute kidney injury and associated systemic signs secondary to accidental oclacitinib ingestion.Series SummaryThree cats ingested large (>100 mg/kg) overdoses of oclacitinib, leading to severe acute kidney injury and associated systemic illness.

pmc-13599908.title: Fragility fractures of the pelvis in the elderly: protocol for an international prospective multicentre observational cohort study
pmc-13599908.creator: Pol Maria Rommens, Alexander Joeris, Mehdi Boudissa, Gregory J Della Rocca, Christian Fang, Maximilian J Hartel, Frank FA Ijpma, Björn Christian Link, Anser Nasir, Philipp Pieroh, Naofumi Shiota, Geoff Wilkin, Daniel Wagner
pmc-13599908.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). IntroductionFragility fractures of the pelvis (FFPs) are low-energy osteoporotic fractures that primarily affect elderly patients. They are associated with substantial morbidity, mortality and healthcare burden, and their incidence continues to rise as the global population ages. Despite the availability of dedicated classification systems and advances in surgical techniques, high-quality evidence to guide optimal management remains limited, and treatment algorithms are not standardised.

uslaw-usc-t25-s402a.title: 25 U.S.C. § 402a — Lease of unallotted irrigable lands for farming purposes
uslaw-usc-t25-s402a.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t25-s402a.description: United States Code, Title 25 (Indians); Chapter 12 (Lease, Sale, Or Surrender Of Allotted Or Unallotted Lands). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. The unallotted irrigable lands on any Indian reservation may be leased for farming purposes for not to exceed ten years with the consent of the tribal council, business committee, or other authorized body representative of the Indians, under such rules.
